text.p: World hour record holder Chris Boardman of Britain overcame cold, rainy conditions to win the prologue of the Tour of Romandie on Tuesday.
Boardman, who crashed in similar conditions during the the prologue of the 1995 Tour de France, showed no fear as he blitzed around the 8.1 kilometre layout in nine minutes 58.06 seconds.
Erik Breukink of the Netherlands was second, 2.26 seconds adrift followed by Dariusz Baranowski of Poland.
Paolo Savoldelli of Italy was fourth and Johan Bruyneel of Belgium fifth.
Switzerland's Tony Rominger, twice winner of the Tour de Romandie who will attempt to reclaim the hour record from Boardman later this year, was 14th, 17.61 seconds behind his rival.
The first stage on Wednesday will be a 168 km test from Kriegstetten to Le Locle.
